title: Sourcing credentials and pricing gate review
summary: Procurement and technical intake to unblock vendor gating: discussed MSA/DPA exceptions, VPC/KMS options for PHI, SLAs for latency/uptime, pricing band approval path and a 30-day pilot plan. Agreed next steps include security docs share, pilot proof-of-concept timeline, and a pricing worksheet for 3-tier usage scenarios.
topics: Latency & SLA targets for clinical workflows
Procurement approval path and required artifacts
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC2 / ISO summary and DPA redline within 2 business days
SE to run lightweight latency benchmark on anonymized sample via hosted token with 48 hour turnaround
Customer to circulate pricing worksheet to finance and respond with preferred band by 2025-05-30
Schedule follow-up with legal and security for MSA exceptions on 2025-05-29

Liam O'Connor: run initial perf benchmark on 10k-token clinical sample (due 2025-05-25)

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-23
Start: 15:30 PT
Duration: 56 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Sofia Patel (CSM), Marcus Yoon (SA); Daniel Reyes (Monarch Procurement), Priya Nair (Security), Tommy Alvarez (Cloud Ops), Linda Park (Legal), Ravi Menon (Eng)

[00:00] Ava Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. quick round robin, i think we have the right folks from Monarch to talk procurement and the technical gating items?
[00:10] Daniel Reyes: Yeah thanks Ava. we wanted to cover MSA/DPA exceptions, and then also confirm what we need for KMS and VPC options because we'll be processing PHI-adjacent clinical notes so need to be careful.
[00:22] Priya Nair: hi, yep. i'm looking for guarantees around key management, audit logs, and clarity on where the data lives. data residency is something we need in scope.
[00:30] Liam O'Connor: quick note — Redwood has three modes: hosted API, dedicated reserved pools, and private VPC deploy. for PHI, most customers go private or dedicated w/ a customer-managed KMS. we can outline both flows.
[00:44] Tommy Alvarez: when you say private, is that full on-prem or VPC with peering? we prefer cloud VPC peering to avoid heavy on-prem ops.
[00:52] Marcus Yoon: yes, we do VPC peering and an optional on-prem appliance for air-gapped sites. for VPC we support customer KMS via KMS integrations and can tie to HSM if required, though there are procurement implications.
[01:04] Linda Park: from legal — can you call out data in transit encryption, who's the data controller/processor, and what the subcontractor list looks like? also DPA redlines, do you accept our standard breach notification window?
[01:18] Ava Chen: great questions. we'll share a DPA redline and a SOC2/ISO summary. breach notifications we typically propose 72 hours, but let's flag that as an open item.
[01:28] Ravi Menon: another practical item — latency. some of our workflows are synchronous patient facing, sub 200ms preferred for short prompts; others are batch. what are realistic SLOs?
[01:40] Liam O'Connor: depends on topology and model. hosted small models can be sub 100ms p50 for small prompt lengths; for the clinical models at 2k tokens, p95 can rise. with Dedicated we can get tighter SLOs because of reserved GPU pools and pinned model variants.
[01:56] Daniel Reyes: procurement will need a pricing band for 3 scenarios: PoC low volume, mid pilot, and anticipated production scale. also we need minimum contract term options and cancellation terms for budget committees.
[02:10] Ava Chen: understood — we'll prepare a pricing worksheet with three bands and show reserved vs hosted delta. also include burst / overage mechanics.
[02:20] Priya Nair: on the security pack — we will need pen test summary, access controls, RBAC, and audit log retention policy. do you have a diagram of network flows?
[02:30] Marcus Yoon: yes, we have a network diagram. we'll include VPC peering flow, NAT, egress constraints, and sample firewall rules. audit logs are exportable to customer SIEM, and retention windows are configurable for dedicated/private.
[02:44] Tommy Alvarez: what's the encryption-at-rest story on hosted? i know with dedicated you can bring your own KMS, but hosted often retains keys. is there a KMS integration for hosted with customer keys?
[02:55] Liam O'Connor: hosted by default uses Redwood-managed encryption but we can discuss bring-your-own-key for certain enterprise tiers; Private/VPC is the recommended route if you need customer-managed KMS for keys at rest.
[03:08] Linda Park: any third-party subprocessors or cloud providers in the chain? we need a full list for the DPA.
[03:16] Ava Chen: we'll include subprocessors list — common ones are cloud infra providers and observability vendors. we'll also call out model hosting partners if used.
[03:24] [03:24] Daniel Reyes: (interrupting) also curious on liability caps when PHI is in play — are you comfortable with carveouts?
[03:32] Linda Park: yes that's a contract ask, we usually propose higher caps for sensitive data.
[03:36] Ava Chen: that's something we'll need legal to align on; i'll flag it as a potential exception.
[03:42] [04:00] Liam O'Connor: technical check — for the pilot, suggested approach: 1) small hosted pilot with anonymized sample for perf and quality, 2) if pass, spin up dedicated pool, 3) then optionally move to VPC. this keeps the procurement friction lower for initial benching.
[04:15] Ravi Menon: ok that sounds pragmatic. do you have costs for the dedicated pilot? like a 30 day reserved window cost?
[04:22] Ava Chen: we'll draft a time-boxed pilot pricing row — typically a 30-day reserved at a discount vs on-demand. i'll show numbers for a modest baseline throughput.
[04:31] Tommy Alvarez: about telemetry — we need token-level cost breakdowns to attribute to product lines. can your console export that?
[04:39] Marcus Yoon: yes, per-route and per-token breakdowns are in Redwood Console. plus tracing hooks and attribution tags you can pass on requests.
[04:47] Priya Nair: one more on compliance — do you support SSO / SAML for admin console and role-based permissions? we need SCIM for user provisioning ideally.
[04:55] Liam O'Connor: yes SSO, SAML, and SCIM supported for enterprise customers; RBAC is customizable.
[05:03] Linda Park: to confirm timeline: we need security artifacts this week, legal wants DPA redline reviewed next week, and procurement will decide on pricing band by next Friday. can you meet those dates?
[05:13] Ava Chen: yes we'll target sending pack by 26th and follow up with legal on 29th.
[05:20] [05:30] Daniel Reyes: last thing — any known export controls or data residency restrictions with model weights if you use third-party models?
[05:38] Marcus Yoon: good call. when we use upstream open models, we control where weights execute; we can restrict to region-specific infra if needed. we'll call out any restrictive license clauses.
[05:47] Ravi Menon: for the perf run, can you run against a redacted dataset of 10k tokens across 100 requests and show p50/p95 and cost per 1k tokens?
[05:58] Liam O'Connor: yes, we'll do that; caveat small differences due to input shape but will provide ballpark and a reproducible benchmark harness.
[06:06] Linda Park: (brief) procurement wants cancellation terms and potential credit for SLA misses — please provide SLA language sample.
[06:14] Ava Chen: we'll include a sample SLA section and outline remediation and credits.
[06:20] [06:40] Sofia Patel: recapping next steps — redwood sends security artifacts + DPA redline, SE runs benchmark, redwood prepares pricing worksheet for 3 bands, and schedule legal/security follow-up.
[06:50] Daniel Reyes: thanks everyone. Priya/Linda we'll sync offline on required docs.
[06:55] Ava Chen: thanks y'all — we'll action items and follow up with calendar invites for the next legal touchpoint.
[07:00] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings — "KV cache" transcribed as "K V cash" at times; "Redwood Dedicated" sometimes shows as "Red wood dedicated" in automated notes. Names slightly garbled near 00:22 for Tom/Tim.
